submitter: silent_hero_logo_readers (follow-on from commission item 2 — the diagnosis code tier, bugs_open/260)
rationale:
THE DEFECT. analysis.ReadSymbolBody is the single door the diagnosis loop's code tier uses to turn a scope entry into source text. It could not resolve either of the two symbol spellings that actually reach it, so it answered 'symbol not found' and the bundle rendered '_(body unavailable — a TOOLING failure)_' in place of the code. The verdict prompt's cite-or-abstain rule then acts on that absence, which is how a run reaches UNVERIFIABLE with the evidence sitting in the index the whole time.

GAP 1 — METHODS. code_symbols_actions.go:598 writes every Go method as '(' + Receiver.Type + ').' + Name, i.e. '(*SagaCoordinator).applyResponseToState'. diagnose_assemble_bundle's scopeFromCodeResults concatenates that column verbatim into a scope entry. spanOf split on the last dot and compared the RAW prefix '(*SagaCoordinator)' against receiverType()'s 'SagaCoordinator' — which can never match. Every one of the index's 1,170 method rows was unreadable.

GAP 2 — PACKAGE-LEVEL VALUES. The analyser has recorded var/const in FileInfo.Values since bugs_open/223 phase 2, and the indexer writes them as rows (1,238 of them). spanOf searched only Functions and Types, so it never looked.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN EDGE CASE. The parenthesised form is the CANONICAL one in this estate. The bundle's own 'Index search results' section renders rows in it ('(*sourceResolver).ensureAssets') and invites the model to name symbols in next_scope; and the LANDMINES entry added 2026-08-11 tells a code_request author in terms: 'Name it `(*Receiver).Method`, or ... you will be told nothing exists and be given no reason to doubt it.' Following our own documented remedy is what triggered the defect. The two producers of this handle grammar had drifted apart and only one side was ever tested — symbolbody_test.go asserts the dotted 'Type.Method' form, which no producer emits.

MEASURED, fleet-wide, over all 460 bundles ever assembled: 321 symbol-read failures across 44 diagnosis runs — 301 receiver-form, 20 package-level values. NOT ONE was a genuinely absent symbol. That is the disconfirming result this could have produced and did not: had the error message ever meant 'you asked for something that isn't there', the fix would not cover it.

WHY AT THE READER, NOT THE PRODUCERS. There are two independent producers of a scope entry — the code-search fallback (our code) and an LLM's next_scope copied from whatever the bundle showed it (not our code). Normalising at scopeFromCodeResults would fix one and leave the other broken. symbolbody.go already owns this grammar by precedent: SplitSymbol and SliceLines were EXPORTED rather than re-implemented for exactly this reason (bugs_closed/163, bugs_closed/189), and 189 was filed at this gate's own direction when a third hand-rolled copy of the split had drifted.

SCOPE. Observability/plumbing repair inside one function, one live call site (diagnose_assemble_bundle_action.go:242). It adds NO prompt text, so the forward concern the architecture seat recorded on commission item 5 — that instructive prompt text in that style could accumulate into a de facto shared vocabulary — is not engaged here. The 145 read BOUNDARY (Output membership decides which PATHS are readable) is untouched: this widens SYMBOL-NAME spelling within an already-analysed file only.

plan.summary: Teach analysis.spanOf the two symbol spellings the code index actually produces: (a) normalise a receiver-qualified name from the canonical '(*T).M' / '(T).M' / '*T.M' forms to the bare receiver type before comparing it against receiverType(), via a new package-local splitReceiver; (b) search FileInfo.Values so package-level var/const resolve at all. No call site changes, no new exported surface, no prompt text. The receiver, once given, must still MATCH — widening the spelling must not widen the match.

edits.rationale: One place normalises the receiver-qualified spelling, so both scope-entry producers (the code-search fallback and an LLM's next_scope) are served by the same grammar owner. Deliberately package-local, not exported: nothing outside this file resolves a symbol name, and an exported helper would be a new shared surface for no caller.

Call splitReceiver instead of the inline last-dot split, and search Values after Functions and Types. Values are searched LAST and only on the bare-name branch, so no existing func/type resolution can move — the change is purely additive to what previously returned not-found.

The regression, written against the pre-fix code and MEASURED failing there first (5 of 7 cases, precisely the broken spellings; the 2 dotted forms passed). Carries negative controls — (*Nope).Greet, (*Helper).Nope, (*Helper).Name (a struct field) — which are the guard that the fix widens the SPELLING and not the MATCH. Those controls were themselves proven load-bearing by mutation: disabling the receiver comparison makes (*Nope).Greet resolve to Greeter's body and the test fails. A premise guard fails loudly if the analyser ever stops recording Values, so the var/const cases cannot pass vacuously.

The shared fixture gains a package-level var and const so the Values half has something to resolve. The two existing tests assert on content, not line numbers, so shifting the fixture's lines cannot silently change what they mean — both were re-run unchanged and stay green.

Both headers stated the old convention — 'A receiver-qualified form ("AnalysisCallGraph.Neighbourhood")' — which is the spelling no producer emits. A reader who trusted that comment would write the one form that used to fail. Corrected to name the index's canonical spelling as the one that actually arrives, and to record that values resolve.
edits.sketch:
-// A receiver-qualified form ("AnalysisCallGraph.Neighbourhood") disambiguates …
+// BOTH spellings are accepted: the code index's canonical
+// "(*AnalysisCallGraph).Neighbourhood" (which is what actually reaches this
+// function — see splitReceiver and bugs_open/260) and the bare form.
+// Package-level var/const resolve by name.

grounded_in: code_symbols_actions.go:598 — the producer, verbatim: `name = "(" + fn.Receiver.Type + ")." + fn.Name` with `kind = "method"`.

symbolbody.go spanOf (pre-fix) — the consumer, verbatim: `if i := strings.LastIndex(name, "."); i >= 0 { wantRecv, wantName = name[:i], name[i+1:] }` then `if wantRecv != "" && receiverType(fn) != wantRecv { continue }`, where receiverType returns `strings.TrimPrefix(fn.Receiver.Type, "*")` — so '(*SagaCoordinator)' is compared against 'SagaCoordinator'.
diagnose_assemble_bundle_action.go:725-746 scopeFromCodeResults — `out = append(out, path+":"+symbol)`, the index's symbol column concatenated verbatim into a scope entry.

Live index spelling census: SELECT CASE WHEN symbol LIKE '(%).%' THEN 'paren-receiver' ... FROM code_symbols GROUP BY 1,2 — 1,170 rows kind='method', ALL paren-receiver; 704 var + 534 const; 3,781 bare func.

Live failure census over every bundle ever assembled: 460 bundles; regexp_matches(body, 'ReadSymbolBody: symbol "([^"]+)" not found') yields 321 failures across 44 correlation_ids — 301 matching '^\(\*?[A-Za-z0-9_]+\)\.', 20 not. All 20 of the remainder were hand-checked and every one is a package-level var or const (ErrWaitingForResponse, workItemTerminalStatuses, templateBlockRegex, reviewRevalidators, maxIngestBytes, …). Zero genuinely-absent symbols.

The motivating run, dbcc4259-ab84-494b-a48b-1df647209a40 (090 on bugs_open/236), verdict UNVERIFIABLE, needed_evidence verbatim: 'The bundle never renders the bodies of persistAwaitingStateWithRetry, processAwaitResponse, or applyResponseToState — only storeActionResult's body and a bare signature line for applyResponseToState are present.' Its iteration-1 bundle shows 9 of 12 in-scope symbols unreadable, and every one of the 9 is receiver-form while all 3 that rendered are bare names.

The index held the evidence the whole time: code_symbols rows for coordinator.go give (*SagaCoordinator).applyResponseToState kind=method lines 2650-2779 body 4,746 chars; persistAwaitingStateWithRetry 2,058; processAwaitResponse 5,619.

The bundle teaches the failing spelling: its own '## Index search results' section renders 'platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/check_image_source_unsatisfiable.go : (*ImageSourceUnsatisfiableCheck).Run' and 'plan_sections_action.go : (*sourceResolver).ensureAssets'.

LANDMINES.md, entry added 2026-08-11 by the diagnosis_schema_visibility lane, verbatim: 'the inverse, for whoever writes a code_request: asking for a method by its bare name is not a narrower query, it is an unanswerable one. Name it `(*Receiver).Method` …' — our own documented remedy for the index-query path is the input the body-read path rejected.

FileInfo.Values exists and is populated: types.go:24 `Values []ValueDef` with the comment 'package-level var and const declarations (bugs_open/223 phase 2)'; a probe against unmodified HEAD logged 'analyser recorded: 2 functions, 2 types, 2 values' while ReadSymbolBody returned 'symbol not found' for both.

Only one live caller, so the blast radius is bounded: grep -rn 'ReadSymbolBody' --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/ | grep -v _test → exactly one call, diagnose_assemble_bundle_action.go:242 (the rest are comments). This matches the correction already recorded in bugs_closed/145 that cmd/assembler is archived reference code outside this module's build.

Fail-then-pass, run against a clean `git archive HEAD` checkout so the shared tree was never mutated: pre-fix the new test fails on exactly (*Helper).Greet, (Greeter).Greet, *Helper.Greet, ErrFixture, MaxFixture and passes the two dotted cases; post-fix all three tests in the package pass, `go build ./...` is clean and `go test ./internal/analysis/ ./platform/orchestration/actions/` is green.
plan.risks:
1. THE ONE REAL JUDGEMENT: WIDENING THE SPELLING MUST NOT WIDEN THE MATCH. The lazy version of this fix — strip everything before the dot and match on the bare name — would pass every positive case and silently break disambiguation, returning some other type's method for '(*Nope).Greet'. The receiver is still REQUIRED to match once given. This is asserted by four negative controls, and those controls were proven capable of failing by mutation (disabling the receiver comparison makes (*Nope).Greet resolve to Greeter's body). Reviewers should press here rather than on the positive cases.

2. DOES THIS CHANGE A GUARANTEE (i.e. is it architecture-scope)? My reading is no, and I would rather be told otherwise than assume. Per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29, an addition to a shared vocabulary needs an RFC when it changes what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES. This does not add a vocabulary item or a capability; it makes an existing function honour the handle format its own producers already emit — the guarantee 'a scope entry naming an analysed symbol yields its body' was always the intent and was simply not met. It also adds no prompt text, so the forward concern recorded against commission item 5 (instructive prompt text accumulating into a de facto shared vocabulary) is not engaged. If a seat disagrees, the contained alternative is to route it as an RFC and leave the fix in place meanwhile, since it is strictly a widening of what resolves.

3. THE 145 BOUNDARY IS UNTOUCHED — and I want this checked rather than believed. Output membership still decides which PATHS are readable; splitReceiver only normalises the SYMBOL NAME after a file has been admitted, and cannot introduce a path. TestReadSymbolBodyRefusesUnanalysedPaths (the 145 regression, including the traversal cases) was re-run unchanged and passes.

4. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE FOR EXISTING CALLERS: bodies that previously came back as 'unavailable' will now render. That makes bundles LARGER, and the body cap (bugs_closed/164) will therefore bite more often — but 164's fix already made an over-cap body SKIP rather than break the loop, and counts omitted-for-coverage separately from unreadable-for-defect. So the failure mode this shifts into is the one that was designed for it. I have NOT measured the new average bundle size — [UNMEASURED], and it cannot be measured until a run happens post-roll.

5. WHAT I HAVE NOT PROVEN. The fix is proven at the unit level and by census; it is NOT yet proven end-to-end, because that needs a diagnosis run against a rolled image. Per bugs_open/236 §3's rule about unfalsifiable zeros, I will not claim the loop is fixed until a post-roll bundle renders a method body — the verification is written down in the bug file as the thing that must happen, not assumed.

6. SCOPE REFUSED. I did not touch the sibling-signature list, which renders `fn.Name` bare and so lists a method under a DIFFERENT spelling from the one the index shows for the same symbol; nor the per-file 10-signature cap that hid the three functions this run needed in a '+79 more'. Both are real and both are separate from this defect. They are recorded in bugs_open/260 as follow-ups rather than folded in.
